messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] error when using Benjamini-Hochberg procedure in "calculateDiffMeth"
parts:
Hi Li,
that's how usually a logistic regression model (binomial GLM) is fit to proportional data. You need those weights to be able to calculate some statistics in the model correctly and to correct for the observations that have low sample size (meaning coverage, similar to number of trials in binomial distribution ). More coverage means more information and these points should have larger effect than points with small coverage. I think it would be unconventional, even incorrect to remove weights from binomial GLM where the response is a proportion.  If you are not interested in coverage and the value it brings to the model, just use a t-test.

Best,
Altuna

Thanks for the explanation. Also, the 0.9.2.5 version now works very well when "slim=F" is set.

messages.author: 487aae5e13177aff
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] error when using Benjamini-Hochberg procedure in "calculateDiffMeth"
parts:
Hi Altuna,

Thanks for your detailed explanation. Yes, I agree with you that we should use t-test when we don't want to include the coverage information. In this case, I should directly use the table generated by unite() and do calculation and t-test in R as methylkit does not provide t-test, am I correct?

Best,
Li

On Friday, February 7, 2014 5:40:43 AM UTC-5, Altuna Akalin wrote:
Hi Li,
that's how usually a logistic regression model (binomial GLM) is fit to proportional data. You need those weights to be able to calculate some statistics in the model correctly and to correct for the observations that have low sample size (meaning coverage, similar to number of trials in binomial distribution ). More coverage means more information and these points should have larger effect than points with small coverage. I think it would be unconventional, even incorrect to remove weights from binomial GLM where the response is a proportion.  If you are not interested in coverage and the value it brings to the model, just use a t-test.

Best,
Altuna




On Fri, Feb 7, 2014 at 6:06 AM, <slee...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Altuna,

Thanks for the explanation. Also, the 0.9.2.5 version now works very well when "slim=F" is set.
Regarding the statistics, do you think it would be better not to consider the "weight" for statistics when "weighted.mean=FALSE" is set? For biological replicates, I think each sample is equally important as long as the coverage is above a certain threshold (already filtered by "mincov" earlier).

Best,
Li


On Thursday, February 6, 2014 1:35:16 PM UTC-5, Altuna Akalin wrote:
this effects only % methylation difference calculation. Statistics are based on logistic regression where a logistic regression model is fit to methylation ratios weighted by their coverages (y), and the treatment vector (x). Then, full model is compared with null model using a likelihood ratio test


On Thu, Feb 6, 2014 at 7:12 PM, <slee...@gmail.com> wrote:
I got it, I didn't notice this switch before. Does this switch affect the statistics? How is the statistics done? Thank you!

Best,
Li

On Thursday, February 6, 2014 1:05:05 PM UTC-5, Altuna Akalin wrote:
if you set weighted.mean=FALSE in calculateDiffMeth(), you should get what you need.

But for the tiles or regions again it sums up number of Cs and coverages which corresponds to a weighted average per region and there is no possibility to do otherwise at the moment.

Best,
Altuna


On Thu, Feb 6, 2014 at 6:58 PM, <slee...@gmail.com> wrote:
Thank you so much Altuna. I am testing it and will let you know how it works.

In addition, I just noticed that the average methylation percentage of a group is calculated using the total Cs and total coverage in the whole group, I think this is good for technical replicates but not good for biological replicates which the methylation% can vary a lot among samples within a group. I wondered if we could also calculate the methylation% for each sample first and then calculate the average value of a group (and also do statistics using the methylation% of each sample)? Thank you!

BTW, what values do you use for the statistics for a tiled window when each group has multiple samples? 

Best,
Li



On Thursday, February 6, 2014 12:38:06 PM UTC-5, Altuna Akalin wrote:
you can try to install the latest development version 0.9.2.5 and see if it works for you.
library(devtools)
install_github("methylKit", username = "al2na",ref = "development",build_vignettes=FALSE)


On Thu, Feb 6, 2014 at 6:18 PM, Altuna Akalin <aak...@gmail.com> wrote:
OK, I figured it out. I will update the development version soon


On Thu, Feb 6, 2014 at 6:04 PM, Altuna Akalin <aak...@gmail.com> wrote:
I can't tell what is wrong, can you send a minimal example, subset of the data and script that goes with that subset and reproduces the error.

Best,
Altuna


On Thu, Feb 6, 2014 at 5:26 PM, <slee...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Altuna,

I got another error: I have no problem to use "calculateDiffMeth" when slim is set to True, however, when I set slim=F, I got the following error message:

> batch1.tile.bh.diff = calculateDiffMeth(batch1.cov10.unite.tile, slim=F, num.cores = 8)
Error in p.adjust(pvals, "BH") : 
  (list) object cannot be coerced to type 'double'

Do you have any clue about it? Thank you!

Best,
Li
